newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil co-op lowers 1997/98 coffee crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: Brazil co-op lowers 1997/98 coffee crop forecast.

text.p: Growers in Brazil's Cooxupe cooperative in Guaxupe, Minas Gerais state, revised downwards their estimate for their 1997/98 coffee crop to 395,065 60-kg bags from a forecast of 433,586 bags in April.
This represented a 49.36 percent drop in relation with 1996/97, Cooxupe said in a statement. The cooperative polled 400 growers.

"One of the reasons that can explain the reduction registered in the July survey with regard to April is the lower yield in the proportion of coffee volume in cherry to processed coffee, due to the irregularity of flowerings," it said.
Cooxupe was the fifth largest exporter in the 1996 calendar year, according to the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation.
The 400 producers questioned own a total 24,678 hectares of coffee and are located in the south of Minas, as well as part of the state's Cerrado region and a portion of Sao Paulo state.
Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry has predicted a national crop of 22 million bags but other forecasts widly differ.
